references.text: Matthew's parallel account of the healing of the paralytic, where Jesus also teaches and the Pharisees are present and ask questions.
Mark's parallel account of the paralytic who was lowered through the roof, where scribes were sitting and watching Jesus teach.
Luke describes how Jesus returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit and taught in the synagogues, forming the background for his ministry in Galilee mentioned in 5:17.

People from all over Judea, Jerusalem, and the coastal region of Tyre and Sidon came to hear Jesus and be healed – parallel to the Pharisees and teachers of the law coming from all over Galilee, Judea, and Jerusalem.
Luke emphasizes that Jesus' power (δύναμις) was known, and people came from everywhere to hear him – background for why teachers of the law came from the whole region.
Jesus knows that a power (δύναμις) has gone out from him when healing the woman with the issue of blood – the same theme of the Lord's power to heal.
Peter proclaims that God anointed Jesus from Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and power (δύναμις), and that he went around doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil.
The prophecy that the Lord's Spirit will rest upon the Messiah and give him power – fulfilled in Jesus' ministry where the Lord's power was with him to heal.
The scribes and Pharisees began to think: "Who is this who speaks blasphemy?" – showing the presence and reaction of the Pharisees introduced in verse 17.
Pharisees and teachers of the law from Jerusalem came to Jesus – the same pattern where religious leaders travel from Jerusalem to investigate Jesus' ministry.
Scribes came down from Jerusalem and accused Jesus – yet another example of religious leaders traveling from Jerusalem to observe Jesus.
